zones.label: Column 1 running header
zones.note: Lexical coverage was cross-checked after independent scan reading against the supplied NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, version 202510 (CC BY 4.0). The scan, not the lexical index, determines this transcription’s spelling, typeface, and lineation.

lines.note: Fanano iro explains this Quaxocu as the colour of a rose or flower. The closing S. is upright; the preceding page’s Qua catchword anticipates this entry.
The next Quaxocu has Fino iro and means the colour of fire, a separate homograph. Its closing S. is upright.

runs.text: Officio que o ſenhor encarrega a al-

lines.note: Quayacu is an office or duty entrusted by a lord to someone; the final al- begins alguem across the line boundary.
Completes al-/guem and introduces Quayacuuo caquru, imposing or assigning an office; the Portuguese translation begins with Impor.

runs.text: o ſenhor algum officio ou cargo.

lines.note: Completes the example: the lord imposes or assigns an office or charge. The printed officio ou cargo has no inserted comma.
Fanano cague explains Quayei as the shadow of roses or flowers. The final ro- continues on the next short line.
Completes ro-/ſas and closes the shadow definition with upright S.; this is a continuation, not an independent headword.
Fino fonouo explains Quayen as a flame of fire. The visible f in fonouo accords with the fire-related Japanese expression.
Quayô, with a circumflex, is explained by Fana, fa: flower or rose, and leaf. The accent is distinct from the unmarked Quayo below.
Quayo is glossed as truces or peace. The Japanese explanation is retained as the visible Voya quabocu; its first form is not silently regularized from the meaning.
Quazocu denotes noble, distinguished people, and the comparison introduced by como is completed by Cungues below.
Cungues supplies the court-nobility comparison within the Portuguese definition. It is printed in italic here, unlike an ordinary roman headword, and no nasal mark is supplied.
Fanano cuqi identifies Quazui as a flower’s stalk or stem; Portuguese Pè is retained with the visible grave accent.
Firocu, firoxi explain Quǒbacu as something broad or extensive. The long-o caron and upright final S. are preserved.
Quǒbun is a great scholar or learned person. Enlargement supports a narrow word division between Grande and letrado; the final S. is upright.

Corrects OCR Quuochi to the visible Quochi: only u and o occur between Q and chi, and no secure accent is visible on this worn headword. Firoqi chiye means broad knowledge; the example starts with clearly accented Quǒ at the line end.
Completes the example Quǒ/china fito without adding an unprinted hyphen, describing a man of great learning.
Firô nagaxi explains Quǒchǒ as broad and long. The two carons in the headword and the circumflex in Firô are separately retained.
Completes the definition with “long”; it belongs to Quǒchǒ, not to the following derived form.
Quǒchǒna is the adjectival form referred back by Idem to the preceding broad-and-long definition.
Quǒchǒni is explicitly marked Aduerb., the adverbial counterpart of the preceding adjective; both printed carons remain.
Restores the opening roman Q misread as italic O. Qina chô gives a yellow butterfly; the first long-o mark is a caron and the second a circumflex, as is the mark in the synonym chô. S. is upright.
Ficarino vchi explains Quǒchǔ as within the light; the caron over u is retained and the Portuguese cla- continues below.
Completes cla-/ridade, the Portuguese word for light or brightness, closing the Quǒchǔ definition.
Quǒcon is equated with Banguei and glossed as evening or late in the day. The tightly printed Atarde is retained; S. is upright.
Firô vôqina explains a very broad and great thing. Restores the visible word division mui larga; the two circumflexes in the synonym are not assimilated to the headword’s caron.
Completes the size definition and introduces Quǒdai mufen, something immense and boundless. The f in mufen is retained rather than mistaken for long s.
Completes im-/menſa, followed by “and infinite,” ending the example of boundlessness.
Are, ſutareta tocoro explains Quǒfai as a ruined or deserted place. The printed comma separates the two Japanese elements.
Completes the definition as a destroyed or uninhabited house. Historical spellings destruida and deſabitada remain; the terminal S. is upright.
Firoi manabi explains Quǒgacu as extensive learning or study. The faint headword accent is retained in accordance with its visible remains and the clear repeated form below.
Completes the learning definition and starts Quǒgacuno chixa, a learned person; the Portuguese Homẽ retains its nasal abbreviation.
Completes the example with “wise and learned,” describing the chixa in the preceding line.
Cuchi firoi cotoba explains Quǒguen as expansive or boastful words, whose character is specified in the next line.
Specifies ostentation and pride, then starts the example with Quǒguen. The original short-s spelling in ostentação is retained.
Completes the example with alternative verbs faqu and yǔ, to utter such words. Removes OCR’s spurious internal space in ſemelhãtes while retaining the nasal mark and the printed alternative marker l.
Von ide explains Quǒgui as the coming or going of a noble person; initial V is part of the historical honorific spelling.
Completes the noble-person gloss and gives the honorific example Goquǒgui naſaruru. Portuguese peßoa and roman Japanese ſ are preserved separately.

runs.text: Ir, ou vir algum ſenhor grande.

lines.note: Translates the example as the coming or going of a great lord, completing the preceding honorific expression.
Quǒgô is a queen or empress, explained by Vono qiſaqi. The synonym visibly has unaccented Vono; no long-vowel mark is supplied merely from the expected word for king.
Quǒ-in concerns the passage of time, explained by Ficarino cague. The interior hyphen is printed; corre has two r types, unlike OCR core. The cosmological wording continues below.
Completes the reference to the primeiro mouel, the first moving sphere in the source’s cosmological vocabulary, and begins the time-and-arrow example Quǒin yano.

runs.text: O tẽpo he como hũa ſeta. ¶

lines.note: Completes Quǒin yano gotoxi, translated as time being like an arrow. A new example starts with Quǒ- at the line end; the nasal abbreviations in the Portuguese remain.

runs.text: Paßar a vida, ou o tempo.

lines.note: Completes Quǒ-/inuo voquru, spending one’s life or time. The printed v in voquru and the physical word division are retained.
Aqiracana ficari explains Quǒmiǒ as radiance or splendour; both long-o marks are carons.
Restores the printed paragraph sign before Quǒmiǒuo fanatçu, to give or emit radiance. The translation continues on the last line of the column.
Completes the expression as emitting radiance from oneself. The joined deſi is preserved, but the visible space before resplandor is restored; the whole continuation is indented.
Quǒmiǒxu is glossed as vermilion from China. The printed final xu and both carons are preserved without substituting a modern pigment name.
Firoqi cado explains Quǒmon as a large gate or entrance. Restores the terminal l in portal, visible just before the right rule.
Completes the large-gateway definition and closes it with upright S.
Firoqi cocoro explains this Quǒqi as a great or broad heart, with its quality specified in the next line. The crop is extended upward to retain the complete initial and accent.
Completes the first Quǒqi definition with “generous”; it does not belong to the following radiance homograph.
Ficari cacayaqu explains the second Quǒqi as shining light or radiance, distinct from generosity. The final S. is upright.
Corrects OCR Q ina qieu to the visible Qina qicu, a yellow chrysanthemum. The Portuguese begins an autumn-flower definition; the internal c is checked against the headword’s qicu.

runs.text: outono aßi chamada de cor amarela.

lines.note: Completes the description of the named autumn flower as yellow; aßi and the historical Portuguese wording are retained.
Gives Quǒqina fito as an example of the adjective applied to a person. Removes the OCR space inside Quǒqina; the wide Q sidebearing does not divide the word.
Describes that person as grand-mannered and generous, linking this adjective with the broad-heart sense rather than the radiance homograph.
Quǒqini is the corresponding adverb, explicitly marked Aduer.; the printed abbreviation is not expanded.
Vǒno gozadocoro explains Quǒqio as the king’s place or residence. The caron over Vǒno is visible here, unlike unmarked Vono in the earlier queen entry.
Completes a-/poſento and specifies the residence where the king is. The unaccented eſta is retained as printed.
Qinafana explains Quǒqua as a yellow flower or rose. The joined Japanese spelling is retained; the crop is extended upward to include the entire opening Q.
The first Quǒquǒ is marked as an adverb and explained by repeated Firoi, “broad.” Its Portuguese adverb is divided Eſpaçoſa-/mente.
Completes the adverb as spaciously or broadly and begins its example. Removes the OCR space after Q in Quǒquǒto without changing the printed carons.
Continues Quǒquǒto xite qiuamo naxi, describing extent without a limit; the Portuguese begins “being very broad and…”.
Completes the example: it is so large that it has no boundary or end. This closes the spatial sense before the radiance homograph.
The next Quǒquǒ, explained by repeated Ficari, concerns radiance. Removes the false OCR word break after Q while retaining the nasal abbreviation at the end of the Portuguese line.
Completes reſplandecẽ-/te, “radiant,” and adds radiance itself as a noun sense.
Qibami votçuru explains yellowing and falling; the example begins Sǒmo-, continued below. Removes the OCR gap inside the headword, retaining the actual example hyphen.

runs.text: O cairem as folhas velhas das

lines.note: Completes Sǒmo-/cu quǒracu and begins the translation: old leaves fall from trees and plants.
Completes the autumn leaf-fall description with trees and herbs in autumn. Historical aruores and eruas remain; the final S. is upright.
Firocu miru and Gacuxǒ explain Quǒran in the sense of wide learning. The Portuguese Le- continues below.
Completes Le-/trado, a learned person, and closes the entry with upright S.
Quǒri is glossed Roxinol, the source’s Portuguese bird name. It is retained without imposing a modern species identification.
Von ide explains Quǒrin as the coming or going of a noble person, parallel to the earlier Quǒgui entry but with the order of the Portuguese alternatives reversed.
Completes peſ-/ſoa nobre, “noble person”; the two long-s characters are preserved across the physical line break.

Quôriǒ introduces an example Quǒriǒno mǒxiyǒ about a manner of speaking. The first headword accent is damaged; the draft’s circumflex is retained provisionally rather than silently made identical to the clear caron in the example.

runs.text: do dẽ falar arrogante, & com clareza ſẽ dei-

lines.note: Completes Mo-/do and describes speech as arrogant and explicit, withholding nothing. The visible nasal mark in dẽ is retained even though ordinary de would be expected; the clause continues after dei-.

runs.text: xar nada no peito, como quẽ diz roncas, & c-

lines.note: Completes dei-/xar and describes leaving nothing unsaid, like boasting. The enlarged right edge has & c followed by a raised, hyphen-like terminal mark; the literal & c- is retained rather than normalized to &c. or joined to the next entry.
Ficari irodoru explains Quǒſai in terms of radiance or the illumination/colouring of a painting. Removes the false OCR gap after Q; the long ſ remains.

runs.text: minação de pintura. ¶ Item, per met.

lines.note: Completes ilu-/minação de pintura and introduces a transferred meaning with ¶ Item, per met. The abbreviation and physical line division remain unexpanded.

Gives the transferred sense “splendid and rich” and starts an example. Enlargement shows a short, nearly horizontal nasal-abbreviation stroke over o in mõ-, not the draft’s caron; this is retained as a tilde, not expanded to n.
Completes mõ-/coni amaru and begins the translation about lustre and rich ornament overflowing. The final ſobe- continues below; the Japanese nasal abbreviation is not converted into a long vowel.
Completes ſobe-/ja and says that the splendour extends above or beyond the roofs, closing the preceding example.
Cacayaqu yoſouoi explains Quǒsǒ as dressing or adorning oneself splendidly. Removes the OCR space inside the headword while preserving its short s and both carons.
Completes the splendid-attire definition and begins a longer example with Quǒsǒ xi. Removes the false Q-space but does not normalize the Portuguese lustroſamente.

Continues the example with atariuo farai, fotoriuo cacayacaſu, expressing an imposing brilliance that clears the surroundings. The f in farai and fotoriuo is retained; the Portuguese translation begins O or-.

runs.text: nato, & luſtro, ou reſplandor era tam grande

lines.note: Completes or-/nato and describes ornament, lustre, or radiance of extraordinary magnitude; the result follows on the next line.

runs.text: que não deixaua chegar aſi a ninguem.

lines.note: Completes the result: the imposing splendour let no one approach. The joined aſi and historical ninguem remain as printed.
Teiuǒno megumi explains Quǒtacu as royal benefactions. The carons are retained and the Portuguese beneficiary/source phrase continues below.

runs.text: del Rey. ¶ Item, Mercès, & fauores de

lines.note: Completes “of the king,” then broadens the meaning to favours and graces from a high-ranking person. The accent in Mercès is preserved.
Completes the general sense with a high and noble person; peßoa remains in the source spelling.
Quǒtei is glossed as king or emperor; the Portuguese emperador is retained without modernization.
Firoqi ſora explains Quǒten as the great, broad sky. No full stop is supplied between headword and synonym where the scan has none; the worn o in Firoqi is not changed to c.

Teiuǒno govon explains royal benefits or favours. Removes the false OCR break after Q; the definition continues onto the following page, while fauores below is a separate catchword, not another body row.

zones.label: Column 2 catchword
zones.note: The italic catchword anticipates the continuation of the final definition on the following page.
